questions.question: What was the Byzantine Empire also known as?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The Byzantine Empire, also known as the Eastern Roman Empire, was the continuation of the Eastern part of the Roman Empire.'
Incorrect. The Byzantine Empire was the eastern part, not the western part, of the Roman Empire.
Incorrect. The Ottoman Empire was a separate empire that eventually conquered Constantinople.
Incorrect. The Holy Roman Empire was a different political entity in Western Europe.

questions.question: In what year did the Byzantine Empire come to an end?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans in 1453 brought the empire to an end.'
Incorrect. 476 is associated with the fall of the Western Roman Empire, not the Byzantine Empire.
Incorrect. 1204 is when Constantinople was sacked during the Fourth Crusade, but the empire was later reconstituted.
Incorrect. 1261 is when Constantinople was recovered, but the empire continued until 1453.

questions.question: What did the citizens of the Byzantine Empire call themselves?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'its citizens used the term 'Roman Empire' and called themselves 'Romans'.'
Incorrect. The term 'Byzantine' was coined only after the empire's demise.
Incorrect. Western Europeans called them 'Greeks', but they did not use this term for themselves.
Incorrect. Ottomans were the people of the empire that conquered Constantinople.

questions.question: Who made Christianity the state religion of the Roman Empire?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'Theodosius I (r. 379â395) made Christianity the state religion.'
Incorrect. Constantine I legalised Christianity but did not make it the state religion.
Incorrect. Justinian I reasserted control over religion but Christianity was already the state religion.
Incorrect. Diocletian instituted the Tetrarchy and is not associated with making Christianity the state religion.

questions.question: Under which emperor did the Byzantine Empire reach its greatest extent?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The Byzantine Empire reached its greatest extent under the reign of Justinian I (r. 527â565).'
Incorrect. Constantine I founded Constantinople but the empire did not reach its greatest extent under him.
Incorrect. Theodosius I was the last emperor to rule both halves, but the empire's greatest extent was later.
Incorrect. Maurice campaigned in the Balkans but the empire's greatest extent was earlier.

questions.question: What happened to the empire in 1204?
options: Constantinople was sacked during the Fourth Crusade
The empire fell to the Ottomans
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The empire was severely fragmented in 1204, following the sack of Constantinople during the Fourth Crusade.'
Incorrect. The empire fell to the Ottomans in 1453, not in 1204.
Incorrect. The reconquest of Italy happened under Justinian I in the 6th century.
Incorrect. The Arab conquests began in the 630s and 640s.

questions.question: What was the name of the Greek settlement on which Constantinople was established?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'Byzantine, derived from Byzantion (Byzantium in Latin), the name of the Greek settlement Constantinople was established on.'
Incorrect. Rome was the old capital of the Roman Empire.
Incorrect. Antioch was a city sacked by the Sasanians in 540.
Incorrect. Carthage was in North Africa and was subjugated by Belisarius.

questions.question: Who instituted the Tetrarchy, a system that divided the empire into eastern and western halves?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'He instituted the Tetrarchy, a system which divided the empire into eastern and western halves.' The 'he' refers to Diocletian.
Incorrect. Constantine I secured absolute power in 324 and rebuilt Byzantium as the new capital.
Incorrect. Julian was a nephew of Constantine I who died in 363.
Incorrect. Valens died at the Battle of Adrianople in 378.

questions.question: What did Constantine I rebuild as the new capital of the empire?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'he rebuilt the city of Byzantium as a new capital that he called 'New Rome' (later named Constantinople).'
Incorrect. Rome was the old capital and was not rebuilt as the new capital.
Incorrect. Antioch was a city in Syria that was sacked in 540.
Incorrect. Carthage was in North Africa and was subjugated in 533.

questions.question: What was the name of the legal code rewritten under Justinian I?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'the legal code was rewritten as the Corpus Juris Civilis, which streamlined Roman law across the empire.'
Incorrect. The Codex Theodosianus was compiled during the reign of Theodosius II.
Incorrect. The Theodosian Walls were fortifications constructed under Theodosius II.
Incorrect. The chrysargyron was a tax that was abolished by Anastasius I.
